query: What does `git rebase --onto` do? Give one short example.
result:
`git rebase --onto <newbase> <upstream> <branch>` takes the commits in `<upstream>..<branch>` and replays them onto `<newbase>` instead of `<upstream>`. Use it to move a branch off a base it was built on, not just to rebase onto its current parent.

Example: `feature-b` was branched from `feature-a`, and `feature-a` has since been merged into `main`. To move only `feature-b`'s own commits onto `main`:

```
git rebase --onto main feature-a feature-b
```

A plain `git rebase main` would also try to replay `feature-a`'s commits, which may already be in `main` under different hashes and cause conflicts.
